I read pp. 158–159 with (4.20), (4.21), (4.35) and Lemma 4.11, and the Lean source. With m = t_s, A = a_L, C = −b_L, exists_local_family_with_margin gives (C.1), a_L > 0, joint smoothness on an open U×ℝ and a uniform margin; uniform_boundary_collar gives δ_∂. All three voters agree on verdict, relation and declarations. Findings 0 and 2 have true premises and Lean-backed recoveries, so they are CONVENTION, not REFUTED. Finding 1 is the only real residue: the paper's one-sided smoothness at η=±1 needs a Whitney/Seeley extension that is not formalized. Lean is otherwise more general (any compact K, B; v_s > 2 only on B). No sorry or axiom in the files read; Lean was not run. Docstrings cite stale numbering.

findings.summary: Lean's uniform margin bounds (A, v−2, P−2, 𝒰(P,J)−v) below by ε. The paper's (C.2) bounds Ψ = (a, v−2, c−v, 2(c−v)²−(v−2)j²) by κ_L. The paper's form follows with κ_L = min(ε, 2ε²).

Lean assumes the data C^∞ on an open set O ⊇ K. The paper assumes smoothness on the closed rectangle, with one-sided derivatives at η=±1 (its stated convention, pp. 25, 39). The two agree only through a Whitney/Seeley extension, which is not formalized.
The headline theorem gives agreement with (a, a·m) on K∩N for an open N ⊇ B, not on a collar of width δ_∂. The companion theorem uniform_boundary_collar converts this to the collar form of (C.3).
